note: The private half of tests/data/state_hash_mutants.json (tools/mutate.py runs it together with the public half): the mutants of files that are not in the public repository, and the ones that only a test that is not there catches. Mutants of a dedicated server's verdict on the state hashes that its seats report (Sequencer::judge_hashes and what a HostSession does with it; docs/NETWORK_PORT.md, 'Sessions' and 'Room'), of the status that counts the seats it dropped, and of the codes that the control interface draws (draw_room_code), for tools/mutate.py (docs/WORKFLOW.md, 'Mutation checks'). Run from the checkout with a configured build folder: python3 tools/mutate.py tests/data/state_hash_mutants.json --keep-going --jobs 1. Every mutant must be caught, and by the tests its test command runs: test_lockstep S2.40 - S2.57 (the rule, whole matches, the seats that held their places, the guards of the verdict, the table that changes between a turn and its answer) and test_server S3.250 - S3.258 (rooms, results, replays, a room that holds seats) and S3.10c - S3.10d (the codes). Not listed on purpose: Sequencer::resume (a host with a seat never has a verdict to forget) and the lines that main.cpp writes to the program's own log (the lines that the rooms hand to RoomManager::take_notices are tested).
